Search query sequences against a database of sequences

Source: R/search.R
search_sequences.Rd

Finds, for every query sequence, the database sequences that it matches with at least `identity` percent identity over at least `coverage` percent of the query length (both strands are searched). This is the search step used inside [clean_reference()]; most users do not need to call it directly.

Usage

search_sequences(
  query,
  database,
  identity = 100,
  coverage = 100,
  max_hits = 100,
  best_hit = TRUE,
  exclude_self = FALSE,
  engine = c("native", "blast"),
  threads = 1,
  k = 12,
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

query

Query sequences: a FASTA file path or a named character vector.

database

Database sequences: a FASTA file path or a named character vector.

identity

Minimum percent identity (0-100). Default 100.

coverage

Minimum percent query coverage (0-100). Default 100.

max_hits

Maximum number of qualifying hits reported per query (best first). Default 100.

best_hit

If `TRUE` (default), queries without any qualifying hit also report their best-scoring non-qualifying hit (with `pass = FALSE`), when one exists.

exclude_self

If `TRUE`, a query is not allowed to match a database sequence with the same ID. Default `FALSE`.

engine

`"native"` (default) or `"blast"`.

threads

Number of CPU threads to use, or `"auto"` to use all available cores but one. Default 1. The search is split across threads on all operating systems (including macOS); results are identical whatever the number of threads.

k

Word length for the native engine index (8-13). Default 12. Smaller values are more sensitive at low identity but slower.

verbose

Print progress messages. Default `TRUE`.

Value

A data frame with one row per reported hit and columns `query`, `subject` (database ID), `identity`, `coverage`, `score` (alignment score for the native engine, bit score for BLAST), `strand`, `qstart`, `qend`, `sstart`, `send`, `pass` (whether the hit meets both thresholds) and `n_pass` (total number of qualifying hits for that query, which can exceed `max_hits`).

Native engine

The default engine is written in C++ and needs no external software. The database is indexed by k-mers (words of length `k`). For each query a q-gram filter computes how many k-mers any qualifying match must share with the query; only database sequences that pass this filter are aligned (banded local alignment with megablast-like scores: match +1, mismatch -2, gap 2.5). Because the filter is derived from the thresholds, no qualifying match is missed when the thresholds are high (identity of about 90 search is an exact containment test and is very fast.

Identity is the number of identical positions divided by the alignment length (as BLAST's `pident`). Upper/lower case and U/T are treated as the same; an ambiguity code (e.g. `N`, `R`, `Y`) is identical only to the same code. BLAST instead scores ambiguity codes as mismatches, so a sequence containing them can be 100 engine but not with BLAST. Coverage is the fraction of the query covered by the best alignment to that database sequence. BLAST's `qcovs` adds together several separate alignments to the same sequence, so coverage values close to the threshold can differ slightly between the engines.

BLAST engine

With `engine = "blast"`, BLAST+ (`makeblastdb` and `blastn`, default megablast settings) must be installed and on the system `PATH`; see [blast_available()]. Identity is `pident` of the best-scoring HSP and coverage is `qcovs`, as in metacleaner 1.x.

See also

[clean_reference()]

Examples

q <- c(q1 = "ACGTACGTTAGCATGCATCGATCGATGCTAGCTAGG")
db <- c(s1 = "TTTTACGTACGTTAGCATGCATCGATCGATGCTAGCTAGGTTTT",
        s2 = "ACGTACGTTAGCATGCATCGTTCGATGCTAGCTAGG")
search_sequences(q, db, verbose = FALSE)
#>   query subject identity coverage score strand qstart qend sstart send pass
#> 1    q1      s1      100      100    72      +      1   36      5   40 TRUE
#>   n_pass
#> 1      1
search_sequences(q, db, identity = 95, coverage = 95, verbose = FALSE)
#>   query subject  identity coverage score strand qstart qend sstart send pass
#> 1    q1      s1 100.00000      100    72      +      1   36      5   40 TRUE
#> 2    q1      s2  97.22222      100    66      +      1   36      1   36 TRUE
#>   n_pass
#> 1      2
#> 2      2
